sessions.title: Introduction
sessions.description: Participants will be introduced to film theory. They will get familiar with the course flow and learning method. They will read and reflect on two articles about structuralism, which will pave the way into understanding the theorists’ approach.

sessions.title: Semiotics
sessions.description: Christian Metz is a founder of the Contemporary film theory. We’ll be introduced to his studies on how film creates meaning like language does. We’ll discuss the similarities and differences between film language structure and linguistic languages. We’ll learn about visual denotations and its significance.

materials.title: Some points in the semiotics of Cinema

activities.description: We’ll discuss the similarities and differences between film language structure and linguistic languages.

sessions.title: Deleuze
sessions.description: Through Metz’s perspective, Gilles Deleuze analyzes his view on film. He categorizes films into two main styles. One is subject to active progression and the other is subject to the feel of time. Participants will reflect on both the narrative styles and Cinematic representations of both styles.

materials.title: The movement image
materials.note: Ch1, Ch2, Ch4; Gilles Deleuze. Week 3

activities.description: Participants will reflect on both the narrative styles and Cinematic representations of both styles.

sessions.title: The apparatus
sessions.description: The question of why cinema is so pleasant for the audience and how we identify with the screen are the topic of discussion. Jean-louis Baudry’s theory relates renaissance to modern art’s influence and engagement with the spectators.

materials.title: Ideological effects of the basic cinematographic apparatus

activities.description: The question of why cinema is so pleasant for the audience and how we identify with the screen are the topic of discussion.

sessions.title: School of Frankfurt
sessions.description: This session is recognition of the cinema social role and its relation to the masses. The participants will discuss nature of Cinema from a Marxist angle. Our reference will be the works of Walter Benjamin in studying the economic influence on Film.

materials.title: The work of art in the age of mechanical reproduction

activities.description: The participants will discuss nature of Cinema from a Marxist angle.

sessions.title: Feminism
sessions.description: Another critical approach in Cinema studies. The analysis of meaning constructed in film from a feminist perspective. The study of Mulvey’s male gaze established in Cinema will be our focus in criticizing women’s role and presentation in Cinema.

data.notes: Method: The course follows a social constructivist approach to learning. The instructor will guide participants in discussing and expressing their understanding of the weekly assigned reading and watch lists. Participants will collaborate and complement their understanding through questioning and elaborating. And by the end of the course, they will be assigned essay writing to reflect on their learning.
